title: A single click opens Home in 236 ms (a fixed 220 ms double-click wait), over the 150 ms panel budget
repro: Click Net once, then Esc. Repeat ×5.
Measure mouseup → panel shown and → first painted frame (renderer clock).
actual: Median 221.4 ms to shown and 236 ms to first paint (n=5, load 2.9–3.2). A double click opens in 21 ms. Closing by clicking Net also waits 233 ms.

title: A single click on Net opens the bar in 254 ms (220 ms double-click wait), above the 150 ms panel anchor
repro: Single-click Net 5 times (close with Esc between)
expected: Panel and caret ≤ 150 ms after the click.
actual: Median 254.4 ms after mouse-up (n=5, load 4.13→3.96; 317 ms after mouse-down); the panel stays hidden for the first 221 ms waiting out a possible double-click; open animation done at 485 ms. A double-click opens in 36 ms, so the wait is the whole cost.

title: CH31/B7.1: no keyboard way to open chat; the click path waits 220 ms for a possible double-click (222 ms to panel)
repro: Look for a shortcut that opens chat (the app menu, global keys)
Click Net and time pointerup → panel shown
expected: a global hotkey opens chat with the caret in the composer in ≤ 150 ms
actual: none exists; the only global keys are the jump key and ⌃⌥⌘R. Single click: 221-223 ms (n=5). Double-click: 0-1 ms. Focus does land in the composer (12/12)

title: CH31: no key opens the command bar — every way in is a mouse action on Net
repro: Enumerate the ways in: click Net, double-click Net, right-click Net → Open Home, ◎ (needs Home open), menu-bar icon menu
expected: A global key opens Home with the caret in the bar (≤ 150 ms keypress → caret).
actual: The only global keys are ⌃⌥⌘J (jump) and ⌃⌥⌘R (record); neither opens the bar. Someone typing in a terminal must reach for the mouse and find Net.

title: Jump-key clash goes undetected: two apps register the same key, both report success, one press fires both
repro: Launch two pet instances (separate profiles) with the same jump key (⌥⌘J)
Check globalShortcut.isRegistered and keyTaken in both; open Settings → Jump key
Post OS-level presses of the key
expected: The second holder reports the key as taken ('Jump key (taken)' + offer the alternative); one press reaches one app.
actual: Both register() → true, keyTaken false, no '(taken)'. 4/4 OS presses fired both handlers within 1 ms (02:28:33, 02:44:28, 02:44:33, 02:44:38) and on the first press both also jumped and wrote the clipboard. Same for ⌃⌥⌘J: a test instance registered it with no '(taken)' while the user's installed pet with that saved key was running; ⌃⌥⌘R (record a short) also registered true alongside, so one ⌃⌥⌘R press would start a recording in both.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'OS key … → shortcut handler fires'
truth: two holders of ⌥⌘J, both instances of this app

title: Setup card's Keys row always says ⌃⌥⌘J, whatever the jump key is
expected: The Keys row shows the active key (⌥⌘J), or 'Off' / 'taken'.
actual: '⌃⌥⌘J jump to who needs you · ⌃⌥⌘R record a short' while the saved and active jump key is ⌥⌘J (renderSetup hardcodes the text).

title: /setup strands the keyboard: the bar disappears, focus is lost after every choice, Done is 20 Tabs away, the card survives close/reopen, and typed keys press setup buttons (pet changed to Sprout)
repro: Press Tab ×6 (⋯, esc, Net, Slime, Cat, Sprout)
expected: The bar stays usable (or focus moves into the card and returns to the bar after Done); typing never changes a setting; Esc leaves setup.
actual: The bar is hidden while the card shows and focus drops to the page. The typed ⏎ pressed the focused "Sprout" button and switched the pet. After Esc and a click on Net the card is still forced, still no bar. Each choice re-renders and drops focus; Done took 20 Tab presses; after Done focus stays on the page, not the bar.
